---
title: "Computational Approaches to Text Analysis"
---

This workshop introduces computational tools for analyzing qualitative data. It is designed for researchers and students with no prior coding experience. You will move through four methods, from manual software-assisted coding to fully automated topic modeling, and practice deciding when each approach is appropriate for a research question.

::: {.callout-note}
## Workshop learning goals

- Understand the difference between software-assisted and computational approaches to qualitative analysis
- Apply word counting, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling to a shared dataset
- Critically evaluate what each method reveals and what it misses
- Connect computational findings to interpretive research questions
:::

## The Dataset

All four exercises use the same dataset: **50 interview paragraphs** from six digital influencers (Alex, Ben, Gina, Linda, Margot, and Otto) discussing ethics, sponsorship, and audience relationships. The interviews were originally published by Renata Gonçalves Curty (UCSB) as part of a UC Love Data Week instructional archive and are available at [zenodo.org/records/18604273](https://zenodo.org/records/18604273). The version used here has been reformatted as a CSV for use across all workshop exercises.

## Workshop Arc

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
<div class="card-route">

### 1 · Software QDA

Overview of qualitative data analysis (QDA) tools and manual coding concepts. In-class exercise with Taguette; take-home practice with QualCoder using a pre-built demo project.

[Open →](instructions/software_qda.qmd){.btn-site}

</div>
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
<div class="card-route">

### 2 · Word Counting

The simplest computational method: count how often words appear. Use Voyant Tools to explore word frequencies in the interview data and consider what frequency reveals and what it conceals.

[Open →](instructions/word_counting.qmd){.btn-site}

</div>
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
<div class="card-route">

### 3 · Sentiment Analysis

VADER assigns each paragraph a score from −1 to +1. Explore the pre-computed results and consider what the distribution tells you and what it leaves out.

[Open →](instructions/sentiment_analysis.qmd){.btn-site}

</div>
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
<div class="card-route">

### 4 · Topic Modeling

BERTopic groups paragraphs by meaning using text embeddings. Explore the output and interpret what the topics suggest about the interview data.

[Open →](instructions/01_simple_explanation.qmd){.btn-site}

</div>
:::
:::
